$$\boxed{\beta_2(E(H))=\psi_{\mathrm{sq}}(E(H))=\Omega(E(H))
=n+\delta(H)=2n-\nu(D(H)).}$$
The TP-to-PZ injection works for arbitrary both-colour feasible representatives. The critical-independent-set construction, matching certificates, and arbitrary- $M$ , white-only zero-TH-expense swaps are sound.I also executed the embedded checker successfully and reproduced its reported JSON field for field.There is one precise verifier limitation: check_certificate does not validate vertex-label domains. I reproduced a malformed external certificate that it accepts because Python permits negative list indices. This does not invalidate the theorem, the inspected certificate-producing algorithm, or the claim that the checker has no missing dependencies. It does require correction before that helper is presented as a sound verifier for arbitrary externally supplied certificates. Details and the exact correction appear below.What I actually auditedI inspected the complete    attached packet: the mathematical note, both Python files, and the embedded output report.Attachment size: 27,251 bytes, 626 lines.Attachment SHA-256:cd18495e858e75c24f702c29d16104bda39fc053849667cb949f3218837738c2Supplied snapshot label: 5044cd735eaddb1acc1e213dbd23f815842b4d63.I did not independently establish that these attached bytes coincide with that Git revision. My source and execution findings apply to the attachment.1. Independent-set deficiency and the matching identitiesThe reduction from arbitrary subsets to independent sets is validHere the neighbourhood of an arbitrary set must mean
$$N_H(X)=\{v:\exists x\in X,\ xv\in E(H)\},$$
which can intersect  $X$ . This is the convention used by both the proof and the code. Defining it explicitly would remove any possible confusion with an exclusively external neighbourhood.For arbitrary  $X\subseteq V(H)$ , put
$$I=X\setminus N_H(X).$$
A vertex of  $I$  has no neighbour in  $X$ . Consequently  $I$  is independent, and
$$N_H(I)\subseteq N_H(X)\setminus X.$$
Therefore
$$\begin{aligned}
|I|-|N_H(I)|
&\ge |X\setminus N_H(X)|-|N_H(X)\setminus X|\\
&=|X|-|N_H(X)|.
\end{aligned}$$
Since every independent set is also an arbitrary subset, the two maxima agree.The left neighbourhood of  $X$  in the ordinary, rung-free double cover is precisely the right copy of  $N_H(X)$ . Hall deficiency therefore gives
$$\delta(H)
=\max_{X\subseteq V(H)}\bigl(|X|-|N_H(X)|\bigr)
=n-\nu(D(H)).$$
There is no bipartiteness assumption on  $H$  in this argument.The fractional-matching identity has the correct factor of twoFor a matching  $F$  in  $D(H)$ , define
$$x_{\{i,j\}}
=\frac12\left(
\mathbf 1_{w_i b_j\in F}+\mathbf 1_{w_j b_i\in F}
\right).$$
At a base vertex  $i$ ,
$$\sum_{j:ij\in E(H)}x_{\{i,j\}}
=\frac{\deg_F(w_i)+\deg_F(b_i)}2\le1.$$
Thus  $x$  is a fractional matching of weight  $|F|/2$ . In particular, choosing both orientations of one base edge is harmless: that edge receives weight one.Conversely, lifting a fractional matching weight  $x_{ij}$  onto each of the two directed copies gives a feasible bipartite fractional matching of total weight  $2\sum x_{ij}$ . Bipartite matching integrality yields
$$\nu(D(H))=2\nu_f(H).$$
Hence
$$\delta(H)=n-2\nu_f(H).$$
The claimed characterization of common value  $n$  follows too. Equality  $2\nu_f(H)=n$  forces every vertex constraint to be saturated, because the sum of all incident weights is  $n$  and each of the  $n$  incident sums is at most one.2. The representative upper bound genuinely covers both coloursLet  $P=V(M)$  and
$$Z=V(E(H))\setminus(T\cup P).$$
With the attachment’s rung counts,
$$|T|-|Z|=2(a-b)+u-v,$$
and, because  $|P|=2|M|$ ,
$$|T|+|M|
=n+\frac{|T|-|Z|}{2}
=n+a-b+\frac{u-v}{2}.$$
TP-to-PZ: the second neighbour is distinct, and the map is injectiveConsider a TP rung. Let its selected endpoint be  $t$ , its occupied endpoint be  $p=\tau(t)$ , and the actual matching partner of  $p$  be  $q$ .Because  $t\notin P$ , we have  $q\ne t$ . Thus
$$\tau(q)\ne p.$$
Applying the adjacency-preserving involution to the actual edge  $pq$  gives
$$t\,\tau(q)\in E(E(H)).$$
The vertex  $t$  already has the neighbour  $p\in P$ . Feasibility therefore forces its distinct second neighbour  $\tau(q)$  outside  $T\cup P$ , so  $\tau(q)\in Z$ . The rung containing  $q$  is PZ.For injectivity, a target PZ rung has exactly one occupied endpoint  $q$ . Its unique actual matching partner determines  $p$ , and then  $t=\tau(p)$  determines the source rung. Thus two source rungs cannot share a target.This argument does not assume that all selected vertices lie on one side. It also does not confuse the fixed rungs with the actual matching edges.TT rungs force the entire neighbouring rungs into ZZLet  $I$  be the indices of TT rungs. If  $i,j\in I$  were adjacent in  $H$ , a selected vertex in rung  $i$  would see its selected rung partner and another selected vertex in rung  $j$ . Hence  $I$  is independent.If  $j\in N_H(I)$ , choose  $i\in I$  adjacent to  $j$ . The selected vertex  $w_i$  already sees  $b_i$ , so it forces  $b_j\in Z$ . Similarly  $b_i$  forces  $w_j\in Z$ . Thus rung  $j$  is ZZ, giving
$$b\ge |N_H(I)|.$$
Combining these facts,
$$\begin{aligned}
|T|+|M|
&=n+a-b+\frac{u-v}{2}\\
&\le n+a-b\\
&\le n+|I|-|N_H(I)|\\
&\le n+\delta(H).
\end{aligned}$$
This proves the stated upper bound for every feasible representative pair.Attainment is correctFor an independent  $I$  attaining  $\delta(H)$ , write
$$R=V(H)\setminus\bigl(I\cup N_H(I)\bigr).$$
The proposed selection is
$$S=\{w_i,b_i:i\in I\}\cup\{w_j:j\in R\}.$$
The only selected edges are the rungs indexed by  $I$ :Independence of  $I$  excludes cross-edges between different selected double rungs.The definition of  $R$  excludes edges from their endpoints to selected vertices indexed by  $R$ .The vertices selected from  $R$  are all white.Therefore  $S$  is a dissociation set, and
$$|S|=2|I|+|R|
=n+|I|-|N_H(I)|
=n+\delta(H).$$
The colouring bridge can be verified directlyThe standard sub-quorum condition concerns a partial colouring and counts only the coloured closed neighbourhood. The indexed primary abstract uses that definition. arxiv.orgUnder that definition, both inequalities used in the attachment have short direct proofs: $\beta_2(G)\le\psi_{\mathrm{sq}}(G)$ . Give every vertex of a dissociation set its own colour. Each coloured closed neighbourhood has size at most two, so its centre alone supplies at least half. $\psi_{\mathrm{sq}}(G)\le\Omega(G)$ . From each colour class containing an internal edge, select one such edge. These edges form a matching because different colour classes are disjoint. From every edge-free colour class, select one vertex  $t$ . Such a vertex has no same-colour neighbour in the original coloured support. The sub-quorum condition then forces it to have at most one coloured neighbour in total. It consequently has at most one neighbour in the retained representative set  $T\cup P$ .The resulting objective  $|T|+|M|$  equals the number of colours. No converse representative reduction is needed.Thus the  $\psi_{\mathrm{sq}}$  equality is mathematically justified without relying on an uninspected external lemma.3. The matching algorithm and its dual certificatesThe iterative augmentation routine is correctThe implementation’s single pass through left roots is valid.Before a root is processed, it is unmatched. Earlier searches reach additional left vertices only by following the existing mate of a right vertex; they therefore cannot match an unprocessed left vertex.For each reached right vertex  $v$ , parent[v] records a search predecessor. If a matched left vertex  $u$  has been reached, its matched right vertex has already been recorded. Consequently the algorithm’s right-vertex visitation check also prevents an incorrect forward traversal of that matching edge.When a free right endpoint is found, reconstruction followsPythonold = left.get(u)
left[u], right[v] = v, uand then continues through old. Every displaced right endpoint is reassigned at the next step. Reconstruction ends at the initially unmatched root and increases the matching size by exactly one.Induction over the processed left vertices gives a maximum matching at termination: after adding one left vertex, the optimum can increase by at most one; an increase is possible exactly when an augmenting path from that new unmatched vertex exists.The production routine is iterative. A safe elementary running-time bound is
$$O\bigl(n(n+m)+m\log n\bigr),\qquad m=|E(H)|,$$
including adjacency sorting. No recursion-depth assumption is needed for this routine.Alternating reachability supplies the advertised certificatesStarting from all unmatched left vertices gives reached sets  $X,Y$ . Every reached right vertex is matched, since otherwise the matching would admit an augmenting path. The matching pairs the reached right vertices with precisely the reached left vertices other than the unmatched roots. Hence
$$Y=N_H(X),\qquad |X|-|Y|=n-\nu(D(H)).$$
The set
$$C=(L\setminus X)\cup Y$$
covers every edge: an edge whose left endpoint belongs to  $X$  has its right endpoint in  $Y$ . Its size is
$$|C|=n-|X|+|Y|=\nu(D(H)).$$
A matching and an equal-size vertex cover certify maximum cardinality independently of trusting the search procedure.For the returned independent set  $I=X\setminus Y$ , Lemma 1 initially gives
$$|I|-|N_H(I)|\ge |X|-|Y|.$$
Equality follows because the right-hand side already equals the global maximum  $\delta(H)$ . The attachment’s “same deficiency” statement is therefore correct; adding this one sentence would make the justification explicit.The empty graph is handled correctly. In particular, the modulo operation in representative_certificate is never reached when  $n=0$ , because there are no TP rungs.4. Arbitrary- $M$ , white-only zero-expense completionThe theorem does not need  $M$  to be maximum, rung-based, or specially oriented.For a bad index  $j$ ,
$$w_j\in T\subseteq Q,\qquad b_j\in P.$$
Write the actual matching edge at  $b_j$  as  $w_i b_j$ . Necessarily  $i\ne j$ , because  $w_j\notin P$ .Symmetry supplies  $w_jb_i$ . Since  $b_j$  is already an occupied neighbour of  $w_j$ , its at-most-one- $P$ -neighbour condition forces
$$b_i\notin P.$$
Thus  $b_i\in Q$ , as required.All swaps are mutually disjointThere are three distinct facts here, and all hold:A bad index has its white vertex in  $Q$ .A mate index has its white vertex in  $P$ , so it cannot be a bad index.Distinct bad indices have distinct mate indices, because  $M$  is a matching.Consequently the index pairs  $\{i,j\}$  are disjoint. Replacing their rungs with
$$w_i b_j,\qquad w_j b_i$$
and retaining every untouched rung produces a perfect auxiliary matching.A selected vertex in a bad rung receives the black terminal  $b_i\in Q$ . A selected vertex in a nonbad rung cannot be a mate-index white vertex, since those are occupied; it retains its black terminal rung partner.Every selected white vertex is therefore in a one-edge terminal path.The tagged-union convention handles common edges correctlyA common actual/auxiliary edge is a two-edge cycle in the tagged union. In the swap construction, the reused edge  $w_i b_j$  lies entirely in  $P$ , while the new edge  $w_jb_i$  is a direct terminal path.Thus no TH path contains any actual edge, and
$$f(N)=0.$$
Nonnegativity of the actual-edge weights gives the matching lower bound  $f(N')\ge0$  for every auxiliary matching  $N'$ , proving
$$\min_{N'}f(N')=0.$$
The argument covers empty, partial, and perfect actual matchings; zero weights; empty selections; and arbitrary variation in nonnegative weights. The white-only hypothesis is used exactly where stated.5. For each enumerated actual matching, the checker calls zero_TH_completion for the maximal feasible white selection
$$T_{\max}=\{w\in Q\cap W:|N(w)\cap P|\le1\}.$$
Its resulting perfect matching pairs every member of  $T_{\max}$  directly with a black terminal, so the same matching certifies every subset of  $T_{\max}$ . That justifies the reported count, but it is not a count of separate function calls.The weight tests do not enumerate heterogeneous assignments. The sampled weights are uniform within each actual matching, including zero and very large integers. Coverage of arbitrary nonnegative weights follows from the independently checked direct-terminal property and the proof, rather than from exhaustive weight sampling.The checker also does not enumerate sub-quorum colourings directly. That part of the conclusion rests on the representative reduction proved above.6. The concrete verifier limitation and its correctionThe following issue is real and was reproduced by execution.Take  $H=K_{1,3}$ , centred at vertex  $0$ . The correct values are
$$\nu(D(H))=2,\qquad n+\delta(H)=6.$$
The production optimum_certificate returns 6, correctly.Nevertheless, the existing check_certificate accepts this malformed dictionary:Python{
    "double_matching": [(0, 1), (-4, 2), (1, 0)],
    "double_vertex_cover_left": [0, 1],
    "double_vertex_cover_right": [0],
    "Hall_left": [1, 2],
    "Hall_right": [0],
    "critical_independent": [1, 2],
    "critical_neighbours": [0],
    "deficiency": 1,
    "dissociation": [1, 2, 3, 5, 6],
    "optimum": 5,
}The mechanism is precise: -4 and 0 are distinct identifiers for the uniqueness test, but h[-4] and h[0] access the same row of this four-vertex graph. The alleged three-edge matching is therefore not a matching on the stated vertex set, although the helper accepts it.Required correction for an external-certificate verifierValidate identifier types and ranges before indexing or accepting any witness. For example, immediately after reading matching, add:Pythondef check_ids(values, limit):
    assert all(type(v) is int and 0 <= v < limit for v in values)

for edge in matching:
    assert len(edge) == 2
    check_ids(edge, n)

for key in (
    "double_vertex_cover_left",
    "double_vertex_cover_right",
    "Hall_left",
    "Hall_right",
    "critical_independent",
    "critical_neighbours",
):
    check_ids(result[key], n)

check_ids(result["dissociation"], 2*n)This is a limitation of the helper as a validator of arbitrary supplied dictionaries. It is not a valid-input counterexample to the attached algorithm: the inspected producer obtains all these identifiers from the appropriate finite ranges.The distinction is therefore:The mathematical certificates are sound.The producer constructs valid certificates.The current test run successfully checks those produced certificates.The helper needs domain checks before it can soundly validate arbitrary external certificates.7. Source attribution, consequences, and  $SF_2$ I inspected Chen’s primary full text. Its definition on printed p. 1078 matches the attachment’s construction, and printed p. 1079 gives the supplied-perfect-matching characterization with paired cross-edges. It also credits Alon for introducing the construction. The attachment’s use of that source is accurate. dml.czI could retrieve the indexed Sahbi abstract, but attempts to fetch the specified original full text failed. I therefore do not claim to have checked the exact original lemma or its numbering. The direct colouring argument above resolves the mathematical dependency for this audit.The additional stated consequences also check out:For bipartite  $H$ , the fibrewise colour choice gives  $E(H)\cong H\square K_2$ .In that case  $D(H)$  consists of two copies of  $H$ , yielding
$$n+\delta(H)=2(n-\nu(H))=2\alpha(H).$$
A fractional perfect matching supplies the claimed fractional square cover: every dissociation set meets each associated four-cycle in at most two vertices.The  $K_3$  example is correct. Its extended cover is  $K_{3,3}$ , and two rows of a real  $3\times3$  sign matrix cannot be orthogonal because their inner product is a sum of three numbers in  $\{\pm1\}$ .Finally, the literal  $SF_2$  test is correct for non-induced two-leaf stars. An outside vertex can be the centre with two selected neighbours, or a leaf adjacent to a selected vertex having a selected neighbour. Checking single deletions correctly detects inclusion-minimality because the forming property is monotone.Those computations establish the reported finite observations only. Neither the representative upper bound nor the zero-expense theorem supplies the missing general upper bound on  $SF_2(E(H))$ . The attachment preserves that separation correctly.
